blanca-rubio.text: Authored AB 1590 (2019), a targeted tax credit to help first-time, low- and moderate-income buyers in disadvantaged communities achieve homeownership; sponsored by the California Association of Realtors.
Voted AYE on AB 130 (housing) on the Assembly floor in March and June 2025, and AYE on SB 71 (CEQA exemptions: transit projects), Sept 2025.
Voted AYE on SB 71 (CEQA exemptions: transit projects) on the Assembly floor, Sept 9, 2025.

Authored AB 789 (2017), letting judges release felony arrestees with three or more failures to appear without an open-court hearing if placed in a court-approved pretrial release program, citing efficiency and less jail overcrowding.
Authored AB 3129 (2018), imposing a lifetime firearm prohibition on anyone convicted of a misdemeanor domestic violence offense.
Voted AYE on AB 1127 (firearms: converter pistols) on the Assembly floor in June and Sept 2025.
Voted AYE on SB 704 (firearms: firearm barrels) on the Assembly floor, Sept 8, 2025.

Authored AB 1654 (2018), waiving PAGA lawsuits in the construction industry for employees and employers covered by a collective bargaining agreement. Authored AB 323 (2019), exempting newspaper carriers from the ABC test for employment status.
Voted AYE on AB 288 (employment: labor organization and unfair practices) on the Assembly floor, June and Sept 2025.
Voted AYE on AB 1340 (transportation network company drivers: labor relations), Sept 9, 2025.
June 2025 statement on immigration raids in Los Angeles County: "In solidarity with our community, we stand vigilant."

source.title: A Response to the Ongoing Situation in Los Angeles County (press release, June 9, 2025)

blanca-rubio.text: Authored AB 1645 (2019), requiring community colleges and CSU to designate a Dreamer Resource Liaison for students exempt from nonresident tuition.

June 2024 on budget talks: it is "imperative that California allocates funding to keep programs like CHIRP, that support children, especially some of the most vulnerable, unaccompanied immigrant children."
Voted AYE on SB 98 (schools: immigration enforcement notification, urgency) on the Assembly floor, Sept 2, 2025.
Voted AYE on SB 81 (health and care facilities: information sharing, urgency) on the Assembly floor, Sept 2, 2025.

Authored AB 1121 (2025), an early literacy bill requiring an evidence-based, phonics-based approach to teaching reading, co-sponsored by the NAACP California Hawaii State Conference, Decoding Dyslexia CA, EdVoice, and Families In Schools.

source.title: NAACP CA-HI Co-Sponsors Assemblywoman Rubio's Early Literacy Bill AB 1121 (March 19, 2025)

blanca-rubio.text: Voted AYE on ACA 8 (congressional redistricting) on the Assembly floor, Aug 21, 2025.
Voted AYE on SB 237 (oil spill prevention: gasoline specifications suspension; CEQA exemptions) on the Assembly floor, Sept 13, 2025.

dan-t-tran.text: Housing priorities: lowering hidden household costs (energy, insurance, fees), supporting first-time homebuyers and renters, cutting permitting red tape that drives up costs, and expanding housing supply, especially workforce housing.

Public safety priorities: supporting local law enforcement with accountability and resources, fighting retail theft and organized crime, strengthening juvenile crime prevention and intervention, and improving emergency response times and mental health crisis response.

Education priorities: strengthening K-12 outcomes (reading, math, career readiness), expanding career technical education and apprenticeships, and partnering with community colleges and local employers.
Campaign is focused on improving public safety, expanding economic opportunity, and protecting constitutional rights, with policies that support law-abiding citizens and strengthen families.

notes: Dan T. Tran has a thin public record: no issues page was reachable (his campaign site returned 404), no endorsements listed, and nothing found on taxes, renters, homelessness, climate, immigration, guns, abortion/LGBTQ+, health care, transportation, or elections. No 2026 endorsements were found for Rubio, and her site gives no issue statements beyond bills.
